title: NATO fighter jet shoots down drone over Lithuania
summary: An Italian NATO fighter jet shot down a drone over Lithuania ‌shortly after midnight on Tuesday morning, the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre said.

image.caption: Debris of what the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre says is a drone shot down by a NATO fighter jet lies on the ground near Pratkunai, Lithuania, on Tuesday in this screengrab from a handout video. (Lithuanian Army/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
An Italian NATO fighter jet shot down a drone over Lithuania ‌shortly after midnight on Tuesday morning, the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre said.
It was not immediately clear if the drone was fired by Russian or Ukrainian forces

The drone, which was likely to have entered from Belarus, was shot ​down near Pratkunai village in southern ​Lithuania, near Kaunas, the second-largest city, the centre's spokesperson said. Its origin had yet to be ​determined, he said.
Military drones ​straying into the ⁠airspace of Russia's neighbours have stoked concerns that Russia's war in Ukraine is spilling over NATO's borders.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said that strikes close to the alliance's territory would drive the trans-Atlantic organization to increase its support for Kyiv. Rutte also pledged to bolster the 32-nation alliance's own defences along its long eastern border with Russia.
Concerns grow over Russia’s incursions into NATO nations

Officials did not say whether ⁠the drone was ⁠believed to be Ukrainian ‌or Russian. In recent months, Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered NATO airspace in the Baltic region. Kyiv says they were steered off course by ⁠Russian signal jamming.
A drone alert was issued earlier in the capital Vilnius and surrounding region.
The Lithuanian army shared video ‌from the site of the crash, showing debris scattered in grass. Some of the parts appeared to be made from wood and some appeared charred.

Fighters ​with the NATO Baltic Air Defence mission have patrolled the skies of ⁠Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia since the Baltic countries joined ⁠the alliance in 2004. The mission's jets shot down stray ⁠Ukrainian ⁠drones over Estonia ​in May, and over Latvia in June and August.
Denmark reports encounter with Russian ship

Separately, Denmark said a Russian frigate fired two flares towards a Danish military helicopter on Monday. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen called the incident "unacceptable" and said it could have endangered human lives.

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the incident was serious but not surprising, calling it part of a ⁠pattern in which an increasingly aggressive Russia has intensified its hybrid warfare against Europe and is testing NATO.
How NATO is tracking airspace threats over eastern Europe
The Russian Embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Baltic Sea region is on high alert after incidents involving gas pipeline ​outages, airspace violations and drone sightings.
Russia has dismissed accusations over such incidents and repeatedly denied carrying out hybrid attacks in Europe.

In fighting on Tuesday, a Russian drone attack ‌killed one person ​and knocked out ​power in parts ​of the ⁠city ⁠of Zaporizhzhia ‌in southeast Ukraine, the ⁠acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said.

As well, the regional governor of Odesa, Oleh Kiper, said that Russia hit port ‌infrastructure in ​Ukraine's southern ​Black Sea region overnight, ‌with residential buildings, ‌logistics facilities and transport infrastructure ​coming under attack.
‌Russian ​forces hit ​a cargo ship ​and ⁠a ⁠ferry ‌carrying ⁠military supplies ‌in ​Ukraine's ⁠port ⁠of Chornomorsk, ⁠the ⁠Russian Defence ​Ministry ⁠said on ⁠Tuesday.

U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday posted on social media that Russia and Ukraine had agreed "not to hit" each other's energy infrastructure. He had earlier called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, saying ​the attacks were causing a shortage of the fuel that is "hurting ​the world."
Trump didn't offer further details on the purported agreement.
Zelenskyy said late Monday that Kyiv was "ready to support de-escalation," but expressed doubts Russia would adhere to such a demand.
With files from the Associated Press
